record.paper_title: Recent Progress and Open Problems in Function Field Arithmetic — The Influence of John Tate’s Work
record.context_brief: Open questions on arithmetic gamma values
record.original_question: What is the arithmetic nature of the values taken by the ℘-adic interpolations associated with the Carlitz-Goss arithmetic gamma function, what algebraic dependence relations hold among the special values of this arithmetic gamma function, and how do these questions extend both to arbitrary global function fields and to the other gamma function discussed in Sections 8.3 and 8.7 of Thakur’s book on function field arithmetic?

evidence.quote: There are still many open questions about the nature of values of ℘-adic interpolations, algebraic dependence relations for the Carlitz-Goss arithmetic gamma function mentioned above as well as their generalizations to arbitrary function fields, and for another gamma function developed in [Tha04, Sec.8.3, 8.7].

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $A = \mathbb{F}_q[\theta]$ be the polynomial ring over a finite field with $q$ elements, with fraction field $K = \mathbb{F}_q(\theta)$, completion $K_\infty$ at the infinite place, and let $\mathbb{C}_\infty$ denote the completion of an algebraic closure of $K_\infty$. The Carlitz factorial is defined on nonnegative integers $n = \sum_i n_i q^i$ (base-$q$ expansion) by $\Pi(n) = \prod_i D_i^{n_i}$, where $D_i = \prod_{j=0}^{i-1}(\theta^{q^i} - \theta^{q^j})$. Goss extended this factorial, via a Carlitz-style interpolation, to an arithmetic gamma function $\Gamma$ defined on $\mathbb{Z}_p$ (with values in $K_\infty$) and to $\wp$-adic interpolations $\Gamma_\wp$ for each finite prime $\wp$ of $A$ (with values in the completion at $\wp$ of an algebraic closure).

(a) Determine the arithmetic nature (transcendence/algebraicity over $K$, and algebraic independence) of the values of the $\wp$-adic interpolations $\Gamma_\wp$ of the Carlitz–Goss arithmetic gamma function at proper $\wp$-adic rational arguments.

(b) Determine all algebraic relations over $\overline{K}$ among the special values $\Gamma(a/f)$ of the arithmetic gamma function, where $a/f$ ranges over proper fractions in $K$.

(c) Extend the above two problems to the analogous gamma functions defined over arbitrary global function fields (i.e., for general base rings $A$ of regular functions on a smooth projective curve over $\mathbb{F}_q$ regular away from one closed point), and to the alternative "geometric" gamma function constructed by Thakur for $\mathbb{F}_q[\theta]$ and its global function field generalizations.
artifact.status_search_result: Significant progress has been made: Anderson–Brownawell–Papanikolas and follow-up work established all algebraic relations among the special values of the Carlitz–Goss arithmetic gamma function for $A=\mathbb{F}_q[\theta]$, and algebraic independence with Carlitz zeta values has been proved. Recent (2024–2025) work interprets $v$-adic arithmetic gamma values as periods of Carlitz motives and proves Chowla–Selberg-type results and algebraic independence in the $v$-adic setting. However, full results for general global function fields and for the geometric (and two-variable) gamma function remain incomplete, so overall the problem complex is only partially resolved.

status_evidence.title: Algebraic independence of arithmetic gamma values and Carlitz zeta values
status_evidence.snippet: All algebraic relations among arithmetic gamma values at proper fractions are determined, and algebraic independence from Carlitz zeta values is proved for A = F_q[θ].
status_evidence.claim: The ∞-adic case for A=F_q[θ] is largely solved.

status_evidence.title: v-adic periods of Carlitz motives and Chowla–Selberg formula revisited
status_evidence.snippet: v-adic arithmetic gamma values are interpreted as v-adic crystalline-de Rham periods of CM Carlitz motives; algebraic independence is established via motivic Galois group techniques.
status_evidence.claim: The ℘-adic interpolation values are now understood in the F_q[θ] case via motivic methods.

status_evidence.title: Algebraic Relations among Special Gamma Values and the Chowla–Selberg Phenomenon over Function Fields
status_evidence.snippet: Aims to determine all algebraic relations among special gamma values over function fields and prove Chowla–Selberg-type formulas.
status_evidence.claim: Extensions to more general function field settings are an active and only partially completed program.
